Essay on reassurance-seeking in OCD; habitual generalizations ('will reliably reassure') and present-tense claims about telehealth business models only.
Medication-series post on Depakote and Abbott's $1.6b False Claims Act settlement; two general calls that criminal pharma practices will continue absent larger consequences.
Fiction dated May 23, 2036 ('This is in the imagined future'), explicitly disclaimed ('None of this is true'); no sincere forward-looking claim. The essay on teaching math is present-tense.

Fictionalized clinical vignette and book excerpt on mentalizing; promotional promises to the reader ('you won't be so worried') and 'In this book, we'll learn them' are not logged.

statements.quote: In the future, we will learn which patients need which stimulator for which part of the brain.
statements.context: Post of 2023-09-20 announcing a pre-print the author co-authored on accelerated TMS with the Brainsway device (real-world sample, greater than 50% remission), compared with Stanford's SAINT/SNT protocol. The author predicts that the field will learn which patients need which stimulator aimed at which brain region.
statements.note: Open-ended call about future personalization of brain stimulation (patient, device, target); no date.

statements.quote: I look forward to the replication of the data.
statements.context: Same post. After presenting the pre-print's accelerated TMS remission data and the SAINT mechanism, the author says he looks forward to replication of the data and to his hypotheses being tested.
statements.note: Anticipation phrasing; may read as a wish rather than an expectation that replication will occur. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: There is a better future for people with depression. It is here. It is brain stimulation. SNT’s methodology is real. This paper’s data is from the real world, supporting my overarching argument that brain simulation is the future of depression treatment.
statements.context: Same post, closing argument. Brain stimulation (Stanford SNT/SAINT and the Brainsway accelerated TMS in the pre-print) is the future of depression treatment; the author says that better future is already here and that oral antidepressants are orders of magnitude worse.
statements.note: Compound: present assertion ('It is here') plus the forward call that brain stimulation is the future of depression treatment. Restates the author's recurring thesis.

statements.quote: Neuroscience and imaging are a crucial part of that better future.
statements.context: Same post, closing paragraphs. After 'Depression can be over. There are many shots on goal,' the author says neuroscience and imaging are a crucial part of the better future for depression treatment (fMRI-guided targeting was mentioned earlier for SAINT).
statements.note: Extends the brain-stimulation-is-the-future claim to imaging-guided neuromodulation; no date.

statements.quote: I have to finish editing a series of papers on psychedelic medicines, but I promise you the data is strong.
statements.context: Same post. After 'Psilocybin also gets depression to remission rapidly,' the author says he has to finish editing a series of papers on psychedelic medicines and promises the data is strong.
statements.note: Author's own publication plan (CONTROL-type); predictive content is that his psychedelic papers are forthcoming and will show strong data.

statements.quote: No world exists in which these criminal practices stop when more profitable to pursue them, even if you get caught
statements.context: Medication-series post of 2023-09-25 on Depakote (divalproex). After recounting Abbott's 2012 $1.6 billion False Claims Act settlement for off-label promotion, and noting Abbott and AbbVie market caps ($170.33b and $269.59b) and share gains since 2000, the author asserts such criminal practices will not stop while they remain profitable, even when caught.
statements.note: General negative call about pharma conduct. The source has a stray space before the period, so the quote ends at 'caught'.

statements.quote: Absent consequences worse than the benefits? We can expect more death and deception.
statements.context: Same post, same closing paragraph. The author argues fines are a scant 0.35% of combined market cap and that only confiscating post-crime profits would deter; absent consequences worse than the benefits, he expects more death and deception from pharma companies.
statements.note: Conditional call ('Absent consequences worse than the benefits'); the author treats the antecedent as the current state.

statements.quote: I think those are going to be useful drugs for a long time ... Oral risperidone? Nope.
statements.context: Medication-series post of 2023-09-27 on risperidone (Janssen-Cilag/J&J, FDA-approved 1994). The author says risperidone and its metabolite paliperidone still have an important role in schizophrenia and bipolar disorder because of the many long-acting injectable formulations; he predicts those LAI drugs will be useful for a long time, while oral risperidone will not ('Nope').
statements.confidence_phrase: I think those are going to be
statements.note: Compound: positive call on long-acting injectable risperidone/paliperidone plus negative call on oral risperidone. Joined across footnote marker 3.

statements.quote: Novel medicines and technologies will be easy to take.
statements.context: Same post. After praising long-acting injectables dosed every 2 weeks to 6 months as real innovation that accounts for human ambivalence about daily pills, the author contrasts oral medicines ('popular because they were easy to sell') with a prediction that novel medicines and technologies will be easy to take.
statements.note: General call about the design direction of future medicines and technologies (adherence-friendly, long-acting); no named product or date.

statements.quote: I suspect does quite a bit more than just that.
statements.context: 173-word update of 2023-10-03 after three nights using the Monarch eTNS trigeminal nerve stimulator for the author's own ADHD. He notes the device is FDA approved as ADHD monotherapy for children 7 through 12 and suspects it does quite a bit more than that.
statements.note: Present-tense belief about efficacy beyond the approved indication; logged for recall because it implies wider future use or evidence.

statements.quote: It is a Brains Stimulation future? Maybe. We will see.
statements.context: Same post, closing line. After noting the company's press release that day about Monarch eTNS approval in Singapore, the author asks whether a brain stimulation future is coming and answers 'Maybe. We will see.'
statements.note: Hedged restatement of the author's brain-stimulation-is-the-future thesis, here for ADHD and trigeminal nerve stimulation.
